claim: Shu, Yu and Mulvey (Downside Risk Reduction Using Regime-Switching Signals: A Statistical Jump Model Approach; arXiv 2402.05272, Journal of Asset Management 2024): an online 2-state jump model on downside deviation (halflife 10) and Sortino ratios (halflives 20, 60), refit every six months on 3000 days, jump penalty chosen monthly by the 0/1 strategy's 8-year validation Sharpe, lifts the S&P 500 Sharpe from 0.48 (buy and hold) to 0.68 (HMM 0.54) on 1990-2023 with 10 bp one-way costs and a one-day delay; MDD -55.2% -> -26.6%, turnover 44%, average exposure 80%.
impact_on_spec: Reproduction target of Stage 2a and the base protocol for every jump-model specification; the reported Sharpe gain is the depth anchor (plan v2 P-1 item 1).
independent_replication: An unverified GitHub replication (I-20260922-03) reports SPY 2008-2025 Sharpe 0.649 -> 0.922 with lower CAGR; a 2025 CBS thesis on factor ETFs finds better but insignificant gains.
limitations: Bloomberg total-return data and GFD bills; no comparison with volatility targeting; selecting the penalty on validation Sharpe can overfit the validation window; equity indices, not levered ETF sleeves.

claim: Princeton research portal record: the jump-model paper is published in the Journal of Asset Management, volume 25, issue 5, pages 493-507 (2024), DOI 10.1057/s41260-024-00376-x.
impact_on_spec: Resolves the open item 5 of I-20261004-06 (journal version exists); the paper is peer reviewed.

claim: Paulsson and Ristic (Copenhagen Business School MSc thesis, 2025, Regime-Based Factor Rotation Leveraging Sparse Jump Models): sparse jump models beat HMMs and plain jump models in simulation; regime-aware factor ETF strategies 2017-2025 delivered higher total returns, Sharpe ratios and lower drawdowns than benchmarks, but the observed performance gains lack statistical significance.
impact_on_spec: Independent recent application on ETFs: effects of this kind are small relative to sampling error in windows of about eight years, so the sleeve thresholds are policy thresholds and a non-pass reads 'underpowered' (power section).
independent_replication: It is itself an independent application of the published method.
limitations: Student thesis; abstract only; Black-Litterman allocation differs from a 0/1 gate.
